idiom_name: Sequelize belongsTo/hasMany with an inferred foreign key column
implementation_notes: Sequelize derives the column from the association call: Order.belongsTo(Customer) puts customerId on the orders table while Customer.hasMany(Order) reads the same column, and options configure foreignKey, allowNull and onDelete/onUpdate (RESTRICT, CASCADE, SET NULL, ...). Eager loading with include resolves the reference in the query; lazy getCustomer() issues the second query only when the attribute is touched. Hand-written mapping over a driver (pg or mysql2 plus explicit column reads) remains justified when you want the SQL visible and no model layer, at the price of writing the resolve step yourself.
pitfalls: Association registration order matters and two hasMany calls without distinct aliases silently overwrite each other, putting the foreign key on the wrong table.
Lazy getCustomer() inside a loop is the N+1; include-based eager loading is the fix, and the association must be registered before the query is built.
Model.sync() and migrations are separate sources of truth: a changed association updates the model but not an existing table unless a migration adds the constraint.
